name: stri_sub
title: Extract a substring from a character vector

origin.description: Extract substrings at code-point index ranges.
origin.usage: stri_sub(str, from = 1L, to = -1L, length, use_matrix = TRUE, ignore_negative_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: Start indexes, 1-based. A negative index counts back from the end. With use_matrix, a two-column matrix of from and to, or from and length when the second column is named length.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: Inclusive end indexes. Ignored when length is passed, and ignored when from is a matrix.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Substring lengths. Zero is an empty string. A negative length is NA unless ignore_negative_length drops that element.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: When TRUE and from is a matrix, read the two columns as the indexes.

arguments.name: ignore_negative_length
arguments.text: When TRUE, drop elements whose length is negative instead of returning NA.

origin.details: Vectorized over str, from, and to or length. Out-of-range indexes are clamped. If from is past to, the piece is empty. A missing string or a missing index yields NA. A leading UTF-8 BOM is removed before indexing.
origin.example:
s <- c("spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam")
stri_sub(s, from = -4)

translation.description: Extract substrings at code-point index ranges.
translation.usage: stri_sub(str, from_=1, to=-1, length=None, use_matrix=True, ignore_negative_length=False)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings. None in a list, and stringi._na.NA, are missing.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: Start indexes. This is from in R. A negative index counts back from the end. A list of length-2 rows, a dict of two columns, or IndexMatrix is a matrix when use_matrix is true. Name the second column length to pass lengths.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: Inclusive end indexes. Omitted when length is passed.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Substring lengths. Zero is an empty string. A negative length is NA unless ignore_negative_length drops that element.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: True only for a single logical TRUE, as in the R wrapper. Anything else reads from_ as a plain index vector.

arguments.name: ignore_negative_length
arguments.text: When True, drop elements whose length is negative instead of returning NA.

translation.details: Indexes are 1-based code points. A start past the end, or an empty string, yields an empty string. A missing string or index yields NA. A leading U+FEFF is removed. If from_ is past to, the piece is empty. Omit length to use to. An explicit length of None is an empty vector, so the result is empty.
translation.value: A list of strings. Missing entries are stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub
s = ["spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam"]
print(stri_sub(s, from_=-4))
